newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key JGB futures end firm, hit 14-month high.
newsitem.headline: Key JGB futures end firm, hit 14-month high.

text.p: Key December Japanese government bond futures continued their rally, hitting a 14-month high for a benchmark futures contract, but profit-taking cut some gains by the close on Thursday.

The December contract opened sharply higher, taking its cue from the London market. Some traders said comments by Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita on the economy after the market closed on Wednesday triggered short-squeezing in London.
Today's rally took the contract to a 14-month high of 122.54 at mid-morning before easing from there. It closed at 122.25, 0.15 up from Wednesday. Volume was 54,663 contracts.
Many traders said buying seemed to gone overboard as the December contract rose above 122.50, the level which beckoned profit-taking.
The Tokyo bourse's reversal in the afternoon hit the bond market, with the key Nikkei index moving into the positive zone.
There were rumours in the market that those who are expected to receive delivery of cash JGBs against the September contract sold the 164th JGBs in large amounts, traders said.
This also sparked worries in the market that the December contract is at high levels, said a trader at a trust bank's securities unit.
But he also added that some institutional investors were placing buy orders, albeit in a cautious manner.
The benchmark 182nd cash JGBs were yielding 2.830 percent at 0720 GMT, up 0.005 from Wednesday.
Many dealers are expecting investors to begin their activity, as cash JGBs will be settled after the end-September half-year book closing from Thursday onwards.
But generally investors are still on the sidelines, and dealers have yet to figure out what they are going to do next.
A 10-year JGB auction, expected some time next week, could be a good gauge of demand, some traders said.
